general_notes: Engineering AS-T 2/MRP (statewide agreement revised 2020, effective Fall 2020; replaced the 2008 agreement; it called for renewal by Fall 2023 but the 2020 document is still the one posted by WSAC and SBCTC). Four pathways: Bio/Chemical; Computer & Electrical; Civil & Mechanical (incl. aeronautical, environmental, industrial); Materials Science & Manufacturing. EvCC offers the Civil & Mechanical AS-T (MRP, 110.5 credits) and Computer & Electrical AS-T (MRP, 105 credits), plus a General Engineering AS-T (90 credits) for majors/schools not covered.

What the MRP guarantees: a student admitted to a participating university 'will be admitted as juniors with all or most prerequisites for the specific engineering major completed', will have lower-division general education 'partially completed', and the university 'will apply up to 111 quarter credits' to the bachelor's degree (subject to its transfer policy). It does NOT guarantee admission to the university or the major: 'Meeting the minimum GPA does not guarantee admission'; programs may require higher overall or course GPAs and minimum grades. Course equivalencies are set by each university.

Minimum: 2.0 cumulative GPA (AS-T 2 rule). Students must apply to graduate at the community college to be awarded the degree. Specialization courses should be chosen for one major at one university - a course useful at one school may not count at another.

Signatories/acceptors of the Engineering AS-T 2/MRP (WSAC 'Schools Accepting DTA/MRPs', updated Aug 2026): UW, WSU, EWU, WWU, Gonzaga, Saint Martin's, Seattle Pacific, Seattle U, Walla Walla. Central Washington University is NOT listed for the Engineering MRP (it accepts AS-T Track 2).

Generic AS-T Track 2 (engineering, physics, atmospheric sciences; 2009, updated 2017; CS removed 2025): junior status and the same priority admission consideration as a DTA holder; does not guarantee admission to the major; GER courses approved by the CC are accepted as GERs but the student must still complete any lower-division general education a DTA holder would not have. Accepted by CWU, EWU, Evergreen, WWU, UW, WSU, Gonzaga, Heritage, Saint Martin's, SPU, Seattle U, Walla Walla.
DTA: the 2014 DTA is being phased out and replaced by a revised 2026 DTA effective September 2026 (WSAC list, Aug 2026); Saint Martin's was not yet listed as accepting the 2026 version.
Private universities apply their own caps: Gonzaga and Saint Martin's accept at most 90-96 quarter credits from community colleges, so a 105-110 credit MRP will not transfer in full there.

STEM 101.title: College Success In STEM
STEM 101.description: Orientation to academic and career opportunities in STEM, with guest speakers from industry and universities and development of skills that promote success in college. Satisfies COLL 101 requirement for new degree seeking students.

STEM 102.title: Equity in STEM
STEM 102.description: Project-based introduction to STEM focusing on problem solving, mathematical reasoning, and communication, built around a team environmental justice project. Covers applied developmental math, units and dimensions, precision and tolerance, teamwork, and basic software.

COLL 101.title: College Success
COLL 101.description: College success strategies including college resources and student services, financing college, time management, learning strategies, choosing a major, and preparing an academic plan.

ENGL 98.title: Intro to College Writing
ENGL 98.description: Writing and revising paragraphs and essays, covering the writing process, diction, grammar, essay patterns, and rhetorical devices. Equivalent to TS 98 and HSC 98; credit cannot be earned in both ENGL 98 and either TS 98 or HSC 98.
ENGL 98.prereq_text: Completion of ENGL 97 or equivalent with a grade of C or higher

ENGL& 101.title: English Composition I
ENGL& 101.description: Writing clear, unified, coherent, well-developed essays of increasing complexity with an emphasis on critical thinking, about or springing from literary or nonliterary texts.
ENGL& 101.prereq_text: Completion of ENGL 98 or equivalent with a grade of C or higher.

ENGL& 235.title: Technical Writing and Research
ENGL& 235.description: Writing memoranda, business letters, and technical documents such as definitions, specifications, proposals, instructions, and analytical reports using primary and secondary research and visual design. Emphasizes audience analysis from lay to expert.
ENGL& 235.prereq_text: Completion of ENGL& 101 with a grade of C or higher.

MATH& 141.title: Precalc I: College Algebra
MATH& 141.description: College-level algebra; first of a two-course sequence for students intending to take calculus beginning with MATH& 151. Functions and graphs, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic functions, conics, non-linear systems, and determinants.
MATH& 141.prereq_text: MATH 96 or equivalent with a grade of C or higher

MATH& 142.title: Precalculus II: Trig
MATH& 142.description: College-level trigonometry; second course in the two-course sequence leading to MATH& 151. Right-triangle and general-angle trigonometry, identities, inverses, trig equations, polar coordinates, parametric equations, and vectors.
MATH& 142.prereq_text: MATH& 141 or equivalent with a grade of C or higher

MATH& 144.title: Pre-Calc I & II: Review
MATH& 144.description: A refresher course in college algebra and trigonometry for students planning to take the calculus sequence beginning with MATH& 151. Polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions, conic sections, and an introduction to vectors.
MATH& 144.prereq_text: One year of high school precalculus or college equivalent; or permission of a math instructor
MATH& 144.placement: One year of high school precalculus or college equivalent; or permission of a math instructor

MATH& 151.title: Calculus I
MATH& 151.description: First course in the calculus sequence: limits, continuity, differentiation and antidifferentiation of algebraic and transcendental functions with applications. For engineering, science, and math majors.
MATH& 151.prereq_text: MATH& 142 or 144 or equivalent with a grade of C or higher

MATH& 152.title: Calculus II
MATH& 152.description: Second course in the calculus sequence: integration and applications of definite integrals (areas, volumes, work, hydrostatic force, centers of mass), polar and parametric calculus, numerical techniques, and improper integrals.
MATH& 152.prereq_text: MATH& 151 with a grade of C or higher

MATH& 163.title: Calculus 3
MATH& 163.description: Third course in the calculus sequence: infinite series, power series and Taylor polynomials, vectors in 2D and 3D, lines and planes, partial differentiation, and double integrals in rectangular and polar coordinates.
MATH& 163.prereq_text: MATH& 152 with a grade of C or higher

MATH& 264.title: Calculus 4
MATH& 264.description: Fourth course in the calculus sequence: triple integrals, vector-valued functions and space curves, directional derivatives and gradients, line and surface integrals, and the theorems of Green, Stokes, and Divergence.
MATH& 264.prereq_text: MATH& 163 with a grade of C or higher

MATH 260.title: Linear Algebra
MATH 260.description: Theory and applications of matrices, linear systems, determinants, Euclidean vector spaces and subspaces, linear transformations and change of bases, and eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
MATH 260.prereq_text: Completion of MATH&163 with a C or higher

MATH 261.title: Differential Equations
MATH 261.description: Introductory ordinary differential equations: existence and uniqueness, first-order linear and non-linear methods, higher-order linear equations, series solutions, systems of equations, and Laplace transforms, with applications.
MATH 261.prereq_text: Completion of MATH&163 or MATH& 264 with a C or higher

CHEM& 140.title: General Chem Prep W/Lab
CHEM& 140.description: Measurements, properties and structure of matter, nomenclature, and weight relations, for students needing chemistry background for the CHEM& 161-163 series. Not intended for students with recent high school chemistry, and does not meet nursing program prerequisites.
CHEM& 140.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 96
CHEM& 140.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 96

CHEM& 161.title: General Chemistry I with Lab
CHEM& 161.description: Properties of matter, atomic theory and structure, periodicity, bonding models, nomenclature, molecular shapes, intermolecular forces, reactions, and stoichiometry. For pre-health professions and all engineering and science majors.
CHEM& 161.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH& 141. One of the following: CHEM& 140 with a grade of C or higher, or one year of high school chemistry with a C or higher within the last one year, or MATH& 152 with a B+ or higher
CHEM& 161.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH& 141; alternative to CHEM& 140/MATH& 152: one year of high school chemistry with a C or higher within the last one year

CHEM& 162.title: General Chemistry II with Lab
CHEM& 162.description: Aqueous reactions (precipitation, acid-base, redox), stoichiometry, thermochemistry, thermodynamics, ideal gases, and properties of liquids, solids, and solutions. For pre-health professions and all engineering and science majors.
CHEM& 162.prereq_text: CHEM& 161 with a grade of C or higher

CHEM& 163.title: General Chemistry III with Lab
CHEM& 163.description: Equilibrium, acid/base and solubility equilibria, buffers, electrochemistry, kinetics, and nuclear chemistry. For pre-health professions and all engineering and science majors.
CHEM& 163.prereq_text: CHEM& 162 with a grade of C or higher.

CHEM& 261.title: Organic Chem W/Lab I
CHEM& 261.description: Chemistry of carbon compounds, with emphasis on structure, nomenclature, reactions, mechanisms, and synthesis of main types of organic compounds.
CHEM& 261.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 and CHEM& 163 with grade of C or higher, or CHEM& 162 with instructor permission.
CHEM& 261.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101; or CHEM& 162 with instructor permission (in place of CHEM& 163)

CHEM& 262.title: Organic Chemistry II with Lab
CHEM& 262.description: Continuation of CHEM& 261: structure, nomenclature, reactions, mechanisms, and synthesis of main types of organic compounds.
CHEM& 262.prereq_text: CHEM& 261 with grade of C or higher.

CHEM& 263.title: Organic Chemistry III with Lab
CHEM& 263.description: Continuation of CHEM& 262: structure, nomenclature, reactions, mechanisms, and synthesis of main types of organic compounds.
CHEM& 263.prereq_text: CHEM& 262 with grade of C or higher.

BIOL& 221.title: Majors Ecology/Evolution
BIOL& 221.description: Mendelian genetics, evolution, biodiversity of life forms, and ecology. First course of the three-quarter majors series for students intending to major in the sciences.
BIOL& 221.prereq_text: CHEM& 161 (or concurrent enrollment) or equivalent, with a grade of C (2.0) or higher. All prerequisites must be taken within the last five years, OR instructor permission.
BIOL& 221.placement: or equivalent; prerequisites must be taken within the last five years, OR instructor permission

BIOL& 222.title: Majors Cell/Molecular
BIOL& 222.description: Metabolism and energetics, structure and function of biomolecules and cells, and applications of biotechnology and molecular biology. Second course of the three-quarter majors series.
BIOL& 222.prereq_text: BIOL& 221 with a grade of C (2.0) or higher and CHEM& 162 (or concurrent enrollment) with a grade of C (2.0) or higher. All prerequisites must be taken within the last five years, or instructor permission.
BIOL& 222.placement: prerequisites must be taken within the last five years, or instructor permission

BIOL& 223.title: Majors Organismal Physiology
BIOL& 223.description: Animal and plant development and physiology, including photosynthesis. Final course of the three-quarter majors series for students intending to major in the sciences.
BIOL& 223.prereq_text: BIOL& 222 with a grade of C (2.0) or higher and CHEM& 163 (or concurrent enrollment) with a grade of C or higher.

PHYS& 114.title: General Physics I
PHYS& 114.description: First course in the one-year algebra-based General Physics sequence (PHYS& 114-116), covering motion, force, momentum, and energy.
PHYS& 114.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101, AND completion of (or concurrent enrollment in) MATH& 142 or MATH& 144 or equivalent.
PHYS& 114.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101; MATH& 142/144 or equivalent

PHYS& 241.title: Engineering Physics I + Lab (PHYS& 231)
PHYS& 241.description: Mechanics. First quarter of the one-year calculus-based sequence (PHYS& 241-243) for engineering and most science majors planning to transfer.
PHYS& 241.prereq_text: MATH& 151 AND PHYS& 114, each with a C or higher, OR passing Physics Placement test, AND eligibility for ENGL& 101.
PHYS& 241.placement: OR passing Physics Placement test (catalog wording is ambiguous whether the test replaces both MATH& 151 and PHYS& 114 or only PHYS& 114); AND eligibility for ENGL& 101

PHYS& 231.title: Engineering Physics I Lab
PHYS& 231.description: Analysis techniques for modeling experimental results and uncertainties, teamwork, scientific and engineering report writing, and independent research skills. Offered concurrently with PHYS& 241, though material does not directly parallel it.

PHYS& 242.title: Engineering Physics II + Lab (PHYS& 232)
PHYS& 242.description: Thermodynamics and waves. Second quarter of the one-year calculus-based sequence (PHYS& 241-243) for engineering and most science majors planning to transfer.
PHYS& 242.prereq_text: PHYS& 241 AND MATH& 152, each with a C or higher.

PHYS& 232.title: Engineering Physics II Lab
PHYS& 232.description: Analysis techniques for modeling experimental results and uncertainties, teamwork, scientific and engineering report writing, and independent research skills. Offered concurrently with PHYS& 242, though material does not directly parallel it.

PHYS& 243.title: Engineering Physics III + Lab (PHYS& 233)
PHYS& 243.description: Electromagnetism. Third quarter of the one-year calculus-based sequence (PHYS& 241-243) for engineering and most science majors planning to transfer.
PHYS& 243.prereq_text: PHYS& 242 AND MATH& 163, each with a C or higher.  Lab PHYS& 233: Completion of MFG T 103 or PHYS 130 with a C or higher.

PHYS& 233.title: Engineering Physics III Lab
PHYS& 233.description: Development and completion of team-designed experiments on instructor-approved topics, producing a publication-quality report. Offered concurrently with PHYS& 243.
PHYS& 233.prereq_text: Completion of MFG T 103 or PHYS 130 with a C or higher.

MFG T 103.title: Machining Lab for Engineers
MFG T 103.description: Introduces machining and manufacturing processes: setup and operation of manual mills, lathes, drill presses, band saws and other shop tools, basic blueprint reading, and an introduction to 3-axis CNC vertical mills.

ENGR 111.title: Intro Engr I: Model/Analysis
ENGR 111.description: Project-based introduction to engineering analysis, problem solving, and mathematical modeling through team hands-on projects. Topics include engineering for sustainability, teamwork, applying math/physics/chemistry, unit systems, and spreadsheets.
ENGR 111.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 96.
ENGR 111.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 96

ENGR& 114.title: Engineering Graphics
ENGR& 114.description: Methods of depicting three-dimensional objects and communicating design information, emphasizing parametric solid modeling software. Freehand sketching develops visualization and design communication skills.
ENGR& 114.prereq_text: Eligibility for MATH& 107 or higher; OR completion of ENG T 100
ENGR& 114.placement: Eligibility for MATH& 107 or higher (alternative to ENG T 100)

ENGR 121.title: Intro to Engineering 2: Design
ENGR 121.description: Second course in the Introduction to Engineering sequence, exploring creativity, teamwork, and communication in innovative design. Includes an introduction to computing, microcontroller programming, and basic parameter optimization through hands-on design projects.
ENGR 121.prereq_text: Completion of MATH& 142 and ENGR 111, OR MATH& 142 and STEM 102, OR MATH& 152, all with a C or higher.

ENGR 201.title: Materials Science
ENGR 201.description: Atomic, molecular, and crystalline structure of materials and its relation to electrical, mechanical, thermal, and chemical properties, with an introduction to materials processing and fabrication.
ENGR 201.prereq_text: CHEM& 161, AND PHYS& 241 (or concurrent enrollment), each with a grade of C or higher

ENGR 202.title: Design of Logic Circuits
ENGR 202.description: Introduction to the basic components of logic circuits, and design and analysis of combinational and sequential logic circuits using modern methods and design tools.
ENGR 202.prereq_text: Completion of MATH& 151, AND either CS& 131 (or concurrent enrollment), or CS& 141 (or concurrent enrollment), all with a C or higher.

ENGR& 204.title: Electrical Circuits
ENGR& 204.description: Introduction to basic circuit and systems concepts, models of resistors, sources, capacitors, inductors, op amps, and transistors, first- and second-order circuit differential equations, and steady-state sinusoidal analysis with phasors.
ENGR& 204.prereq_text: Completion of ENGR 121, AND PHYS& 243 (or concurrent enrollment) with a C or higher.

ENGR 205.title: Electric Circuits Lab
ENGR 205.description: Laboratory applications of electrical circuit principles and instrumentation, including measurement of transient and steady-state circuit responses.
ENGR 205.prereq_text: ENGR& 204 with a grade C or higher, OR concurrent enrollment.

ENGR& 214.title: Statics
ENGR& 214.description: Fundamentals of engineering statics using vector notation in problem solving. Scientific calculator required.
ENGR& 214.prereq_text: ENGR 121 or concurrent enrollment, AND PHYS& 241 or concurrent enrollment, AND ENGL& 101 or concurrent enrollment, each with a C or higher

ENGR& 215.title: Dynamics
ENGR& 215.description: Kinematics and dynamics of particles, systems of particles, and rigid bodies, including energy and momentum methods.
ENGR& 215.prereq_text: Completion of MATH& 152 AND ENGR& 214, both with a grade of C or higher.

ENGR 216.title: Integrated Comp Aided Design
ENGR 216.description: Advanced CAD for engineering design and analysis: surface and combined surface/solid modeling, advanced part/assembly techniques, CAD-based structure/flow/motion analysis, and complete design documentation.
ENGR 216.prereq_text: Completion of ENGR& 114 and ENGR& 214 with a C or higher.

ENGR 220.title: Mechanics Breaking Lab
ENGR 220.description: Hands-on mechanical behavior of materials and experimental stress analysis: tension, impact, fatigue, and torsion testing, stress waves, strain gages, and combined stress analysis, with data analysis and report writing.
ENGR 220.prereq_text: ENGR& 225 with grade of C or higher, or concurrent enrollment

ENGR& 224.title: Thermodynamics
ENGR& 224.description: Thermodynamic properties of matter and first- and second-law analysis of engineering systems, including energy interactions, device performance and efficiency, power cycles, and refrigeration cycles.
ENGR& 224.prereq_text: Completion of CHEM& 162, AND MATH& 152, AND PHYS& 241, all with a C or higher.

ENGR& 225.title: Mechanics of Materials
ENGR& 225.description: Introduction to the mechanics of solids: stress, strain and their relationships, torsion, and bending.
ENGR& 225.prereq_text: Completion of MATH& 152 AND ENGR& 214 with grade of C or higher.

ENGR 240.title: Applied Numerical Methods
ENGR 240.description: Solving engineering and science problems with modern computing tools, selecting computational algorithms and communicating results, with an introduction to MATLAB programming for numerical computation.

CS& 131.title: Computer Science I C++
CS& 131.description: Software development in C++ covering data types, variables, control structures, modular design, pointers, dynamic memory, and arrays, with an introduction to memory management and object-oriented programming.
CS& 131.prereq_text: Completion of CS 110 or ENGR 121 with a C or higher

CS 132.title: Computer Science II C++
CS 132.description: Advanced C++ software development emphasizing object-oriented concepts and fundamental data structures: recursion, encapsulation, inheritance, templates, polymorphism, and abstract data types such as stacks, queues, linked lists, and binary trees.
CS 132.prereq_text: Completion of CS& 131 with a C or higher.

CS& 141.title: Computer Science I Java
CS& 141.description: Basic programming concepts for engineering and science problems in Java: classes, objects, methods, variables and types, control structures, arrays, strings, and collections and iterators.
CS& 141.prereq_text: Completion of CS 110 or ENGR 121 with a C or higher.

CS 143.title: Computer Science II Java
CS 143.description: Advanced Java software development emphasizing object-oriented concepts and fundamental data structures: recursion, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and abstract data types such as stacks, queues, linked lists, and binary trees.
CS 143.prereq_text: CS& 141 with a C or high

CS 233.title: Data Structure and Algorithms
CS 233.description: Advanced data structures and fundamental algorithms in C++, introducing complexity analysis and asymptotic notation and emphasizing design, analysis, and comparison of algorithmic solutions.
CS 233.prereq_text: Completion of CS 132 with a C or higher

ECON& 201.title: Micro Economics
ECON& 201.description: Supply and demand factors in production and prices, emphasizing the economic behavior of firms in regulated and unregulated environments and international trade. Prepares students for upper-division microeconomics and managerial economics.

ECON& 202.title: Macro Economics
ECON& 202.description: Study of the national economy: national income, growth, fiscal and monetary policy, inflation, unemployment, money supply, globalization, and business-cycle theories. ECON 101 may be substituted for ECON& 202 in professional/technical business degree programs.

BUS& 101.title: Intro to Business
BUS& 101.description: An introduction to the American business system in a global, Internet-influenced economy, covering ethics and social responsibility, management, finance, human resources, entrepreneurship, and marketing.

MATH 86.title: Essential Intermediate Algebra
MATH 86.description: Introductory course in mathematical reasoning, focusing on real-world applications and conceptual understanding.
MATH 86.prereq_text: MATH 76 or equivalent with a grade of C or higher

MATH 96.title: Intermediate Algebra for Precalculus
MATH 96.description: Intermediate algebra for students headed into science, business or engineering: functions, linear systems, polynomials, rational expressions, exponents and radicals, quadratics and exponential functions.
MATH 96.prereq_text: MATH 86 or equivalent with a grade of C or higher

general_notes: Transfers enter UW engineering majors through the College of Engineering 'capacity-constrained' pathway: apply to UW (UW Admissions transfer application) AND separately to each engineering major via the Engineering Application (uapp.engr.washington.edu) once eligibility requirements are met. Admission to a major is competitive and not guaranteed; capacity varies by year.

Autumn start: UW application Feb 15; major application opens late March, due April 5; major decisions early May; UW decisions by late June. Spring start (Bioengineering, Chemical Engineering, and Allen School CS/CompE): UW application Dec 15; major application due Jan 15 (5 pm PT); decisions mid/late February. Missing the UW deadline means you cannot apply to an engineering major.

Autumn-start majors: Aeronautics & Astronautics, Civil, Computer Engineering (Allen School; also spring), Electrical & Computer Engineering, Environmental, HCDE, Industrial, Materials Science, Mechanical. Spring-only: Bioengineering, Chemical Engineering. Winter is not an entry point for engineering majors.

College-wide minimums: grade of 2.0 or higher in each required course and a 2.50 GPA in prerequisites/cumulative (Allen School states no minimum GPA). Required to apply = done by the department deadline; enrollment requirements = done before the first quarter in the major.
Credits: College guideline is at least 45 relevant college credits; departments set their own (CEE and MSE 55, A&A 60, Allen School 30). Most transfers need about two years at a community college.

World language / CADRs: since winter 2023 applicants, transfers with 40+ transferable quarter credits at application do not have to meet the College Academic Distribution Requirements (including world language). Below 40 credits, CADRs apply; each quarter of a college language counts as one year of high school (two years needed).

Associate degree: not required for engineering transfer admission (A&A page says so explicitly). The DTA gives junior standing but UW states it is 'not an admission agreement'. UW signed the 2020 Engineering AS-T Track 2 MRP (four pathways); completing it does not guarantee admission. Max 90 lower-division transfer credits apply to the UW degree.

WA community and technical college first-choice admission rates (2023/2024/2025, %): A&A 40/67/33; BioE 40/60/75; ChemE 100/100/72; Civil 92/100/94; CompE & CS 31/29/28; ECE 92/80/71; EnvE 100/100/100; HCDE 60/83/71; IE 100/100/100; MSE 100/100/100; ME 80/79/62. A&A, BioE, CompE/CS, ECE, HCDE, ME are labeled 'historically more constrained'. Applying to several eligible majors is encouraged.
EvCC chemistry: CHEM& 162 and 163 transfer as UW CHEM 152 and 162 only if BOTH are taken; CHEM& 162 alone = CHEM 1XX. Any major that needs CHEM 152 effectively needs the full CHEM& 161-163 sequence.

EvCC programming: UW intro CSE is Java. CS& 141 = CSE 142 (4) + 1XX (1) and CS 143 = CSE 143; CS& 131/CS 132 (C++) transfer only as UW 1XX. UW's CSE 142/143 were replaced by CSE 121/122/123 in 2022-23; departments accept 142/143 as noted.

Equivalency caveat: the Engineering, Math and Physics sections of the UW Equivalency Guide for Everett could not be read (page too long for the fetch tool). Mappings for MATH&, PHYS&, ENGR& and EvCC MATH 260/261 come from UW's statewide tables (UW Bothell STEM transfer table) and the UW guide rows for other colleges. These mappings differ between colleges, so confirm each EvCC row in the guide or MyPlan before publishing.
UW 'Transfer Thursday' advising sessions are recommended for prospective transfers.
